title: Blood-vessels are arranged for minimum effort and minimum wall-surface

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Blood-vessels are arranged for minimum effort and minimum wall-surface

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The form and arrangement of blood-vessels are such that circulation proceeds with a minimum of effort and a minimum of wall-surface (and hence of friction).

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The general principle is that the form and arrangement of the blood-vessels is such that the circulation proceeds with a minimum of effort, and with a minimum of wall-surface, the latter condition leading to a minimum of friction and being therefore included in the first.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Branching of arteries”. Scope: vertebrate vascular systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Optimization can be formulated, but the intended constraint set and trade-off between effort and surface are underdetermined. Open networks permit restricted tests rather than a decisive vertebrate-wide result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct vascular networks, calculate pumping-power and wall-area costs, and compare observed networks with constrained alternative branching networks. Closeness to a Pareto optimum would support, while feasible networks dominating both costs would refute, the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most datasets capture only part of a vascular tree.

“Minimum” depends on unspecified anatomical and functional constraints.

discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Downloadable arterial reconstructions contain the geometric variables an optimality test needs. Thompson's minimum of effort is broad enough that several cost functions remain compatible with the same trees, which is why discriminating power stays moderate. The data can reject crude nulls in humans and leave the vertebrate-wide claim only partly tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On reconstructed arterial trees, compare observed radii, lengths and branching against the minimum-power, minimum-surface prediction (Murray scaling and short paths) and against alternatives such as space-filling or constant daughter-parent ratios. Support would be a lower combined cost than those rivals across beds; a consistent excess cost would refute the optimality claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available trees are concentrated in the human brain and large vessels.

Effort can be operationalized as hydraulic power, wall surface, or endothelial shear, and those costs are not minimized by the same geometry.
